title: KV: batch-aware residency controller and hardware-aligned fragment reshaper
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We observed two correlated production failure modes under high-concurrency, mixed-size request workloads: (1) fragmentation of the KV cache that increases per-request allocation overhead and induces extra spill IO, and (2) spill storms that amplify tail latency when many requests simultaneously miss in cache and trigger large DMA transfers. This PR introduces two coordinated features to address those problems: a batch-aware residency controller that adapts eviction thresholding and proactive compaction to ongoing batching behavior, and a hardware-aligned fragment reshaper that reduces fragmentation and kernel stalls by re-aligning fragmented allocations onto device-friendly grain sizes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a batch residency controller that observes continuous batching statistics (current batch size distribution, P95 batch latency, token-per-request histograms) and dynamically adjusts per-tenant eviction pressure and soft-residency windows. The controller uses a lightweight EWMA of batch tail latency to decide when to relax evictions (to avoid unnecessary spill during transient load spikes) versus when to compress aggressively.
- Implements a fragment reshaper in the KV allocator: on low-risk background compaction windows the reshaper migrates small adjacent fragments into hardware-aligned slab segments (128B/256B/4KB depending on device preference), reducing scatter DMA and CUDA kernel launch overhead for reassembly. Alignments are tunable and can be disabled.
- Adds a spill throttle that gates spill IO based on a latency budget tied to batch SLOs. When throttle is active, large low-priority spill tasks are rate-limited and smaller top-off refills are prioritized to maintain throughput while bounding P95 latency.
- Introduces new metrics and alerts: kv.batch_size_p95, kv.residency_pressure, kv.fragmentation_score, kv.spill_throttle_active, kv.reshaper_moved_bytes. These are surfaced in the Console and used by the rollout monitor.
- Adds feature flags and runtime knobs: kv.enable_batch_residency (default true), kv.residency_sensitivity (low/medium/high), kv.reshaper_alignment_bytes, kv.spill_throttle_target_ms.

Design decisions:
- Controller is conservative by default: it biases toward avoiding unnecessary spikes in spill IO (favoring slightly higher memory usage) because spill storms are much more damaging to tail latency in our tests.
- Reshaper runs opportunistically during idle compaction windows and is tenant-rate-limited to avoid interfering with normal request latency. Data migration is done in-place where possible; we fall back to copy-and-swap for fragments that cross slab boundaries.
- Throttle is additive to existing backpressure; it never drops requests but can reclassify spill tasks as background.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/kv/residency/controller.go (core controller, heuristics)
- runtime/kv/allocator/reshaper.go (fragment identification + migration engine)
- runtime/kv/allocator/alignment.h (alignment helpers for device kernels)
- runtime/kv/spill/throttle.go (throttle policy & pacing)
- runtime/kv/metrics/registry.go (new metrics)
- runtime/kv/tests/* (unit and integration tests for controller/reshaper)
- benchmarks/kv/batch_residency_bench.go (bench harness)
- docs/ops/kv-tuning.md (operator-facing knobs and rollout steps)

Commits (summary):
- 1) initial batch residency controller prototype + unit tests
- 2) hardware-aligned fragment reshaper + allocator hooks
- 3) spill throttle implementation and scheduler integration
- 4) metrics and Console wiring + small dashboard
- 5) benchmark harness and perf numbers
- 6) tests and race fixes (concurrency guard for migration)
- 7) docs, changelog, and feature flag defaults

Behavioral compatibility: All changes are behind runtime flags where non-disruptive defaults are selected. Existing tenants will see improved tail latency under high load; behavior under low load is effectively unchanged. There are no schema changes persisted on disk.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Unit tests: 48 new unit tests cover eviction heuristics, migration safety, and throttle behavior.
- Integration: Simulated multi-tenant replay with mixed request sizes (1–4096 tokens) for 60 minutes; validated no regressions in correctness and no deadlocks.
- Perf: On our lab cluster (A100-equivalent nodes) with a 32-tenant synthetic workload mimicking production burst patterns: median token latency unchanged, P95 latency reduced by 7% overall, spill IO volume decreased by 22%, fragmentation_score decreased by ~18% after 30 minutes of reshaping. Microbenchmarks show a 9% reduction in kernel stall time attributable to reduced scatter DMA.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable kv.enable_batch_residency and kv.spill_throttle at 10% traffic for 48h with active observability.
- Monitor kv.spill_throttle_active and kv.batch_size_p95 for regressions.
- If stable, enable reshaper gradually (it does heavier background work): 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks.

Backwards compatibility & safety: all migrations are reversible via runtime flag. Reshaper moves are logged and can be rolled back. No on-disk format changes.

Notes for reviewers: look closely at the concurrency guards in reshaper.go (we replaced a coarse global lock with per-segment CAS guards) and at race mitigation in the spill scheduler. Bench harness includes a comparison script in benchmarks/kv/compare.sh to reproduce numbers locally.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

review_comments: Evan Chen (2026-02-19): Nice approach. Two quick asks: 1) please add a short-circuit when batch size is 1 so we don't pay controller overhead for single-request paths; 2) can you add a microbenchmark that isolates the reshaper cost and reports CPU time?
Priya Nair (2026-02-19): Added short-circuit and microbenchmark in commit 3. Also added a comment in reshaper.go explaining the per-segment CAS strategy.

Marta Liu (2026-02-20): The per-segment CAS looks good but I'm worried about fragmentation_score oscillation during sustained medium load. Can we make the reshaper back off if fragmentation_score doesn't improve after N iterations?
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Added exponential backoff when reshaper sees <2% improvement after 3 runs; included test to validate backoff behavior.
Diego Alvarez (2026-02-22): CI flaked on one race detector test; it looks related to migration_helpers. Found a missing atomic when clearing a 'moving' bit. Please fix.
Priya Nair (2026-02-22): Fixed missing atomic and re-ran race detector; all green now.
ci_checks: Benchmarks: pass (bench harness ran, results attached)

release_notes: Improved KV cache resilience under high-concurrency workloads via a batch-aware residency controller and a background hardware-aligned fragment reshaper. Expect reduced P95 latency and lower spill IO for mixed-size request workloads. New knobs: kv.enable_batch_residency, kv.residency_sensitivity, kv.reshaper_alignment_bytes, kv.spill_throttle_target_ms.
notes_for_ops: Default rollout is safe but monitor kv.spill_throttle_active and kv.fragmentation_score. If spikes in memory usage are observed, reduce kv.residency_sensitivity or disable the reshaper via kv.reshaper_enabled=false. Use docs/ops/kv-tuning.md for recommended tuning values.
bench_results_summary: On lab cluster with synthetic 32-tenant bursty workload: P95 latency -7%, spill IO -22%, fragmentation_score -18% after 30min, kernel stall time -9%. Detailed bench outputs in artifacts/benchmarks/923456/*.log
